source_text:
Πᾶσα δόξα καὶ πλατυσμὸς ἐδόθη ὑμῖν, καὶ ἐπετελέσθη τὸ γεγραμμένον: Ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔπιεν, καὶ ἐπλατύνθη, καὶ ἐπαχύνθη, καὶ ἀπελάκτισεν ὁ ἠγαπημένος.
ἐκ τούτου ζῆλος καὶ φθόνος, καὶ ἔρις, καὶ στάσις, διωγμὸς καὶ ἀκαταστασία, πόλεμος καὶ αἰχμαλωσία.
οὕτως ἐπηγέρθησαν οἱ ἄτιμοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐντίμους, οἱ ἄδοξοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐνδόξους, οἱ ἄφρονες ἐπὶ τοὺς φρονίμους, οἱ νέοι ἐπὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους.
διὰ τοῦτο πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἡ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη, ἐν τῷ ἀπολιπεῖν ἕκαστον τὸν φόβον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ πίστει αὐτοῦ ἀμβλυωπῆσαι, μηδὲ ἐν τοῖς νομίμοις τῶν προσταγμάτων αὐτοῦ πορεύεσθαι, μηδὲ πολιτεύεσθαι κατὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῷ Χριστῷ, ἀλλὰ ἕκαστον βαδίζειν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ τῆς πονηρᾶς, ζῆλον ἄδικον καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἀνειληφότας, δἰ οὖ καὶ θάνατος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
thought_title: From prosperity to faction: the fall of Corinth
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, recalling how their former glory and prosperity fulfilled Scripture, and how envy then produced faction and every evil.
pass_a_gloss: All glory and enlargement was given to you, and was fulfilled the [thing] written: He ate and drank, and was enlarged, and grew fat, and kicked the beloved [one]. From this envy and spite, and strife, and faction, persecution and disorder, war and captivity. Thus were stirred up the dishonored against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders. Through this far away is righteousness and peace, in the [act of] each [one] abandoning the fear of God and in his faith becoming dim-sighted, nor in the lawful [things] of his commandments walking, nor conducting [oneself] according to the [thing] fitting for Christ, but each [one] walking according to the desires of his heart, the wicked [heart], unjust and impious envy having taken up, through which also death entered into the world.

lemmas.gloss: were stirred up, were raised up
to become dim-sighted, to see poorly
to conduct oneself, to live as a citizen

choices.why: The glossary requires 'envy' for ζῆλος, the root cause of the Corinthian strife.
The glossary requires 'faction' for στάσις, the divisive uprising in Corinth.
The glossary requires 'elders' for πρεσβύτεροι, the duly appointed leaders of the Corinthian church.
The verb means to kick with the hoof, as a fattened animal does; 'kicked' preserves the physical, violent image from Deuteronomy 32:15.
The noun denotes instability and confusion in civic or communal life; 'disorder' fits the list of social evils and pairs naturally with 'persecution'.
The verb means to see weakly or dimly; 'become dim-sighted' keeps the metaphor of failing spiritual vision in his faith.

bible_refs.note: Ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔπιεν, καὶ ἐπλατύνθη, καὶ ἐπαχύνθη, καὶ ἀπελάκτισεν ὁ ἠγαπημένος

pass_b_english: You were given every glory and abundance, and what is written was fulfilled: "He ate and drank, and grew large and fat, and the beloved kicked." (Deuteronomy 32:15)
From this came envy and spite, strife and faction, persecution and disorder, war and captivity.
So the dishonored were stirred up against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders.

For this reason righteousness and peace stand far away. Each one has abandoned the fear of God and become dim-sighted in his faith. Each one no longer walks in the lawful paths of God's commandments or conducts himself as is fitting for Christ. Instead, each one walks according to the desires of his own wicked heart, having taken up unjust and impious envy, through which death entered the world.

polish.changed: Clarified the implied subject of the commandments as God's, broke the long final sentence into shorter units, and made the repeated 'each one' explicit so the sequence of accusations is easier to follow aloud.
Clarified pronoun referents and sentence flow, kept all claims and Scripture references exactly, and ensured the modern reader can follow who is being addressed and what each term means.

notes.why: In this era, bishop/elder/presbyter were often the same office; inconsistent terms confuse the hierarchy.
notes.fix: Add a note explaining the overlapping use of these terms.

notes.why: Minor, but 'young' vs 'children' may blur the specific age groups being addressed.

last_rejected.quote: having taken up unjust and impious envy, through which death entered the world
last_rejected.source_quote: ζῆλον ἄδικον καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἀνειληφότας, δἰ οὖ καὶ θάνατος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον
last_rejected.why: δἰ οὖ = 'through which' (neuter singular, referring back to ζῆλον/ἔρις/στάσις complex, or the whole disposition). The English 'through which' could ambiguously refer to 'envy' alone. But ζῆλον is masculine, δἰ οὖ is neuter—likely refers to the whole situation or to 'envy' as abstract concept. The sense is not wrong. However, ἀνειληφότας is masculine plural accusative, agreeing with implicit subject 'each one' (ἕκαστον...βαδίζειν). The English 'having taken up' correctly captures the participial construction. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter's own analysis confirms no error; 'through which' adequately renders δἰ οὖ and 'having taken up' correctly renders ἀνειληφότας.
